lines.trans: All the paintings were painted by me personally.
Any of them can be purchased.
The money will go to charity.
And this right here is my pride.
It is called 'Ex-Husband.'

Which Victor Petrovich?
Because he is a coward and a liar.
They called me from work, I will go.

meanings.note: Abstract feminine noun formed with the Slavic suffix '-ость' ('-ness, -ity') from the corresponding adjective. Common feminine noun meaning 'charity' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: На кухне отеля всегда есть благотворительность.
examples.trans: In the hotel kitchen there is always charity.

meanings.note: бывший мэр = the former mayor; бывшая жена = ex-wife

examples.text: Мне нужно немножко поработать с бывшим мэром.
examples.trans: I need to do a little work on the former mayor.

meanings.note: Singular only. Abstract feminine noun formed with the Slavic suffix '-ость' ('-ness, -ity') from the corresponding adjective. Common feminine noun meaning 'pride' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: He is the pride of our family.

examples.text: Слушай, тут пишут: «Гордость России! Наконец-то кто-то за народ!»
examples.trans: Listen, here they write: 'Pride of Russia! Finally someone is for the people!'

examples.text: Мои повара быстро сломают вашу гордость.
examples.trans: My cooks will quickly break your pride.

meanings.note: plural only: there is no singular in everyday use

examples.trans: The money is on the table.

Core Russian prep meaning 'until, before; up to' in everyday speech.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'втра').

examples.text: Позвони мне вечером. Договоримся на завтра.
examples.trans: Call me this evening. We'll arrange something for tomorrow.

meanings.note: emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Искусство войны = The Art of War. Prefix 'ис-' ('out from within') marks extraction or exhaustion (stem 'кусство'). Common neuter noun meaning 'art, skill' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Read The Art of War, by Sun Tzu!
She loves modern art very much.
This is a real culinary work of art!

meanings.note: In questions. Core Russian det meaning 'what; what a' in everyday speech.
in exclamations: какой грязный! = how dirty!

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'painting, picture' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: На кухне картины Дали и Ван Гога.
examples.trans: Paintings by Dalí and Van Gogh in the kitchen.
Beautiful paintings hang in the museum.

examples.text: У вас очень плохая картина по безопасности.
examples.trans: You have a very bad picture regarding safety.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'liar' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Потому что он трус и лжец.
examples.trans: Because he is a coward and a liar.

examples.text: На кухне отеля всегда есть лжец.
examples.trans: In the hotel kitchen there is always liar.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Аникеев лично сюда приезжал, и что?
examples.trans: Anikeev came here in person, and what?

examples.text: Пятнадцать лет мы просим новое здание! Аникеев лично сюда приезжал, и что?
examples.trans: For fifteen years we've been asking for a new building! Anikeev came here in person, and what?

meanings.note: В любой момент = at any moment. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('any').

examples.text: Любая обезьяна эти выборы выиграет! Ты что, хуже обезьяны?
examples.trans: Any monkey will win this election! What, are you worse than a monkey?

meanings.note: Asking permission. Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.
Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: Can I go and have a look?

meanings.note: Agrees with the thing owned. Core Russian det meaning 'my, mine' in everyday speech.
Мой муж = my husband. Common masculine noun meaning 'husband' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Nina, pour your husband a drink. We've got something to celebrate!

meanings.note: + prepositional: на сайте. Core Russian prep meaning 'on, onto; for' in everyday speech.
+ accusative: на второй срок. Core Russian prep meaning 'on, onto; for' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: of things, places, films: 'как называется ...?' = what is ... called?

examples.trans: The operation is called Golden Yard.

examples.text: Товарищ генерал, операция называется Золотой ярд.
examples.trans: Comrade General, the operation is called Golden Yard.

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'писать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to write', paired with 'писать'.

examples.text: А зачем? Я сам сделал так, чтобы он его написал.
examples.trans: And why would I? I'm the one who made him write it.

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'слаждаться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'enjoy'.

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и наслаждаться вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and enjoy on time.

examples.text: На нашей кухне все умеют наслаждаться.
examples.trans: In our kitchen everyone knows how to enjoy.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates

Prefix 'об-' ('around, about') marks encirclement or comprehensive action (stem 'манывать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to deceive, to cheat', paired with 'обмануть'.

Prefix 'об-' ('around, about') marks encirclement or comprehensive action (stem 'манывать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to deceive, to cheat', paired with 'обмануть'.

examples.text: Потому что она простая. Её все обманывают.

examples.text: Ты что, с первого раза не понимаешь?
examples.trans: What, you don't understand the first time?

meanings.note: + dative: 'позвони мне' = call me. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'звонить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to call, to phone', paired with 'звонить'.

examples.text: Позвони мне вечером. Договоримся на завтра.
examples.trans: Call me this evening. We'll arrange something for tomorrow.

meanings.note: On foot. Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to go (set off)', paired with 'идти'.

examples.trans: Can I go and have a look?

meanings.note: In потому что. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'тому').
Потому и = that's exactly why. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'тому').

examples.text: Я устал, потому что много работал.
examples.trans: I'm tired because I worked a lot.
I'm at home because I'm ill.

meanings.note: + в + prepositional. Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'знаться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to confess, to admit', paired with 'признаваться'.

examples.text: Никак, я тебя на понт взяла. А ты сейчас сама призналась.
examples.trans: No way at all, I called your bluff. And you just confessed yourself.

meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'нести'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to bring (on foot)', paired with 'приносить'.

examples.text: А я вот вам чаю с сушками принёс.
examples.trans: I've brought you some tea and bread rings.
What did you bring into the flat?

meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'обрести'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'acquired / bought'.

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и приобрести вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and acquired on time.

examples.text: На нашей кухне все умеют приобрести.
examples.trans: In our kitchen everyone knows how to acquired.
